pharm: Prodrug split by colonic bacteria into 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA), which acts locally as a topical anti-inflammatory in the bowel, and sulfapyridine, which is systemically absorbed and contributes to antirheumatic effect and most of the sulfonamide-related toxicity.
quick: UC: 3-4 g/day in divided doses (start 1-2 g); maintenance 2 g/day. RA: build to 2 g/day
Take in evenly divided doses, preferably after meals, with adequate fluids
Generally continued with folic acid supplementation; weigh benefit
Caution; sulfapyridine passes into milk - avoid in ill/premature/G6PD-deficient infants
Caution; maintain hydration to prevent crystalluria
CBC and LFTs frequently early on; urinalysis; observe G6PD-deficient patients for hemolysis
summary: Sulfasalazine is a sulfonamide-aminosalicylate prodrug used for mild-to-moderate ulcerative colitis (and as adjunct in severe disease and to maintain remission) and, as a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug, for rheumatoid arthritis. It can cause serious and sometimes fatal hypersensitivity, blood dyscrasias, hepatic and renal injury; G6PD-deficient patients must be watched for hemolytic anemia, and reversible oligospermia can occur in men.
indications: Mild to moderate ulcerative colitis and adjunctive therapy in severe ulcerative colitis
Prolongation of the remission period between acute attacks of ulcerative colitis
Rheumatoid arthritis in patients with inadequate response to NSAIDs (enteric-coated/DMARD formulation)
Polyarticular-course juvenile rheumatoid arthritis in children who responded inadequately to NSAIDs (enteric-coated formulation)

dosage.d: 3 to 4 g daily in evenly divided doses (intervals <=8 hours); may start 1-2 g/day
Initial 40-60 mg/kg/day in 3-6 divided doses; maintenance 30 mg/kg/day in 4 doses
Start 0.5-1 g/day, increase weekly to 2 g/day in 2 divided doses (max 3 g/day)

admin: Take in evenly divided doses, preferably after meals, with intervals not exceeding 8 hours
Maintain adequate fluid intake to prevent crystalluria and stone formation
Use the enteric-coated (DR) formulation for rheumatoid arthritis to reduce GI intolerance
Obtain baseline CBC, LFTs and renal function; repeat CBC and LFTs frequently early in therapy
Discontinue immediately for signs of toxicity or hypersensitivity, and stop while awaiting blood test results if a dyscrasia is suspected
Note that sulfasalazine may color urine and skin orange-yellow and may stain soft contact lenses
moa: Sulfasalazine is a prodrug. In the colon, bacterial azoreductases cleave it into 5-aminosalicylic acid (5-ASA, mesalamine), which acts locally as a topical anti-inflammatory agent in the bowel wall, and sulfapyridine, which is absorbed systemically. The therapeutic benefit in ulcerative colitis is largely attributed to the 5-ASA moiety, while the anti-inflammatory/immunomodulatory action in rheumatoid arthritis is less well defined and may involve sulfapyridine and effects on folate metabolism and immune cells.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to sulfasalazine, its metabolites, sulfonamides, or salicylates
Porphyria (sulfonamides can precipitate an acute attack)
monitor: Renal function and urinalysis; signs of hemolysis in G6PD deficiency

preg: Sulfasalazine crosses the placenta. It is often continued in inflammatory disease during pregnancy because untreated disease poses risk, but it impairs folate absorption, so supplemental folic acid is recommended. Weigh benefit versus risk and counsel accordingly; use near term carries a theoretical risk of neonatal kernicterus.
lact: Sulfapyridine is excreted in breast milk in significant amounts. Use with caution; avoid in mothers of ill, premature, or G6PD-deficient infants because of the risk of hemolysis and bilirubin displacement.
renal: Use only after critical appraisal in renal impairment. Maintain adequate hydration and alkalinize urine if needed to prevent crystalluria and stone formation; monitor renal function and urinalysis.
hepatic: Use only after critical appraisal in hepatic impairment. Hepatotoxicity, including fatal hepatic necrosis and hepatitis, has been reported. Monitor liver function tests, and discontinue for signs of liver injury such as jaundice.

moderate: Folic acid and folate-dependent drugs (sulfasalazine reduces folate absorption)
interactions.food: Take after meals to reduce GI intolerance; maintain adequate fluid intake.
interactions.alcohol: Limit due to additive hepatic and gastrointestinal effects.

Renal function and urinalysis with microscopy

pk: GI effect over days; antirheumatic benefit over several weeks
Sulfapyridine plasma peak ~10 hours after a dose

pearls: Observe G6PD-deficient patients closely for dose-related hemolytic anemia
Serious blood dyscrasias (agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia) and hepatic injury can be fatal - check CBC/LFTs frequently early and act on sore throat, fever, pallor, purpura or jaundice
Prodrug: 5-ASA delivered locally to the colon; sulfapyridine drives most systemic toxicity
Causes reversible oligospermia/male infertility and reduces folate absorption (supplement folate)
Harmless orange-yellow discoloration of urine/skin; can permanently stain soft contact lenses
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Toxicity correlates with serum sulfapyridine concentration. Features include nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and in advanced cases drowsiness and convulsions. Manage with gastric lavage/emesis and catharsis, alkalinize urine, and force fluids if renal function is normal; restrict fluids/salt and treat appropriately if anuric. Monitor serum sulfapyridine.
